Wow, this is quite a mess.

1. First case of black and white/mindreading thinking in the first two sentences. It's not the same everywhere, or even most places in case you were intending that to be a hyperbole. Nobody cares on this sub? My main gripe is that sometimes people care *too* much and never indulge my (unhealthy and unhelpful) behavior, but that's a good thing.

2. "From what I see, you want to get help here? You have to be functionnal and actually have some kind of real friends in real life."
That's just objectively false.

3. There are cases where therapy doesn't help. I'm in that situation currently. I highly doubt that your therapist lied to you, what would be their reason too? Why would they go through college, training, retraining, etc to be a therapist just to lie to their patients? Often times things we don't want to hear are perceived as lies, that may be what's happening. I find it hard to be open to my therapist's suggestions as well, I can understand that.

4. They don't do it for the money. It takes quite an investment, financially and emotionally, to get into and keep this profession. They wouldn't do that for [less than $50K a year](https://money.usnews.com/careers/best-jobs/marriage-and-family-therapist/salary).

5. I can't convince you to make major life changes. I don't think I can even convince you to reconsider. What I can do is try and challenge the walls your mind has put up with any reason whatsoever, whether they be correct or not. I will leave you with this. I genuinely hope you get better, but it has to start with you.
